tasks.title: A floor where you have to hide
tasks.why: The owner's idea for a later floor: when its entity is angry enough, a voice tells the crew to hide, the lights go out, music starts, and anyone found during the search dies
todo: Owner's words (2026-11-16): 'if the entity is aggro'ed enough, it kicks off a voice that tells players to hide. If they're found before timer goes off, they're killed. Otherwise, the entity follows it's normal rules. (only move when looking etc) The level goes dark, creepy music starts playing, and players have to find a place. You'll have to research how to make a good ai bot that explores rooms so that the challenge is actually challenging. Staying visible and just running away kills you. Once count is finished, moving faster than creep drains health maybe?'

My reading, to confirm with the owner: (1) an anger level rises with noise (sprinting, calls, readings); (2) at the top, the announcer starts a count (about 20 s), lights go out, music starts; (3) when the count ends a search runs for a set time: the entity checks rooms and hiding places; anyone it finds is taken; moving faster than a creep costs health; (4) when the search time is up it goes back to its usual rule. Hiding places come from the props (lockers, under beds, cupboards, behind curtains).

Research before building (one agent, written up in docs): how games make a searcher that feels smart and fair. Start from occupancy / probability maps (the searcher keeps a belief of where players could be and checks the likeliest spots), last-known-position search, a director that nudges it toward players without telling it exactly (Alien: Isolation's two-part design), and hiding-spot checks with tells so a hidden player can hold their breath. Must stay deterministic from the seed and simulate hundreds of rounds: good hiders usually live, runners die, nobody dies to pure luck.

Fits the existing rules: the entity is heard before seen; the instrument could pay most for a reading taken from a hiding place while it searches nearby; a found player goes down rather than out, with something to do within seconds.

Owner (2026-11-16, later): 'Clicking the elevator should trigger a hiding sequence, so you have to survive one last time before making it to freedom.' So on this floor calling the car always starts one last count-and-search; the car arrives when the search ends. It is this floor's version of the Clinic's blackout while waiting.
